title: Poker, con artists and the psychology of risk and deception, with Maria Konnikova, PhD

sentences.en: Have you ever been conned, or maybe you know someone who's fallen for a scam?
sentences.zh: 你有没有被骗过，或者认识什么人上过当？

sentences.en: Do you wonder why intelligent people join cults, or give money to psychics, or get sucked into Ponzi schemes?
sentences.zh: 你是否好奇为什么聪明人会加入邪教、给灵媒送钱，或者陷入庞氏骗局？

sentences.en: Have you ever gone to Las Vegas or Atlantic City and wondered what it might feel like to play poker for high stakes?
sentences.zh: 你有没有去过拉斯维加斯或大西洋城，想过玩高额赌注的扑克是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Are the big winners lucky, skillful, or both?
sentences.zh: 那些大赢家是靠运气、靠技术，还是两者兼有？

sentences.en: Do you feel like your brain is too cluttered with unnecessary facts?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得自己的大脑里塞满了没用的事实？

sentences.en: Would you like to know how to better organize your mind?
sentences.zh: 你想知道如何更好地整理思绪吗？

sentences.en: Are you wondering what on earth these questions have to do with each other?
sentences.zh: 你是不是在想，这些问题到底有什么关联？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: At APA, we often say that psychology is relevant to every aspect of life, and that studying psychology can better equip you whatever path you choose.
sentences.zh: 在APA，我们常说心理学与生活的方方面面息息相关，无论你选择什么道路，学习心理学都能让你如虎添翼。

sentences.en: Our guest today is a living, walking, and writing example of that.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾就是这方面一个活生生的、行走的、写作的典范。

sentences.en: Maria Konnikova has a PhD in psychology from Columbia University, but she works primarily as a journalist, except for the many months she spent studying and playing Texas Hold'em,
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·康尼科娃拥有哥伦比亚大学的心理学博士学位，但她的主要职业是记者，除了她花了好几个月时间研究并打德州扑克的那段日子，

sentences.en: eventually becoming an international poker champion and winning over $300,000 in tournament earnings.
sentences.zh: 她最终成为了一名国际扑克冠军，在锦标赛中赢得了超过30万美元的奖金。

sentences.en: She's also studied con artists, from fortune tellers to the purveyors of the Nigerian prince scam, to three-card Monty players on the streets of New York.
sentences.zh: 她还研究过骗子，从算命先生到“尼日利亚王子”骗局的始作俑者，再到纽约街头的“三张牌”赌徒，都有涉猎。

sentences.en: And she has applied her knowledge of psychology to understanding and explaining how to think like Sherlock Holmes and how not to think like Dr. Watson.
sentences.zh: 她还将自己的心理学知识应用于理解和解释如何像夏洛克·福尔摩斯那样思考，以及如何避免像华生医生那样思考。

sentences.en: Konnikova has written three best-selling books,
sentences.zh: 康尼科娃写过三本畅销书，

sentences.en: Mastermind, How to Think Like Sherlock Holmes,
sentences.zh: 《大师思维：像福尔摩斯一样思考》，

sentences.en: The Confidence Game, and her latest, The Biggest Bluff.
sentences.zh: 《欺骗的艺术》，以及她最新的作品《最大的虚张声势》。

sentences.en: Her writing has been featured in Best American Science and Nature Writing, and has been translated into more than 20 languages.
sentences.zh: 她的作品曾入选《美国最佳科学与自然写作》，并被翻译成20多种语言。

sentences.en: She's also a contributing writer for The New Yorker magazine, and host of the podcast series The Grift, which explores con artists and the lives they wreck.
sentences.zh: 她还是《纽约客》杂志的特约撰稿人，并主持了播客系列《骗局》，该节目探讨了骗子及其摧毁的人生。

sentences.en: Maria Konnikova, welcome to Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·康尼科娃，欢迎来到《心理学谈话》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Just reading your biography could make anyone feel like a goldbricker, which is actually a type of work-avoiding grifter that you describe in The Confidence Game.
sentences.zh: 光是读你的简历就足以让人觉得自己是个“金砖骗子”（goldbricker），这其实就是你在《欺骗的艺术》中描述的那种逃避工作的骗子。

sentences.en: And I didn't even mention that you did your graduate work at Harvard, where you studied psychology, creative writing, and government.
sentences.zh: 而且我还没提到你在哈佛大学读过研究生，在那里你学习了心理学、创意写作和政府学。

sentences.en: Were you just trying to make up your mind what to be when you grew up?
sentences.zh: 你当时是不是在纠结长大后要做什么？

sentences.en: No, I think I always knew I wanted to be a writer.
sentences.zh: 不，我想我一直都知道自己想成为一名作家。

sentences.en: According to, well, I don't know if it's apocryphal, but I don't remember it because I was five years old or so.
sentences.zh: 根据——好吧，我不知道这算不算传闻，因为我当时才五岁左右，记不清了。

sentences.en: But according to my family, I informed everyone over dinner when I was about five that I was going to be a writer when I grew up.
sentences.zh: 但据我家人说，我五岁左右在晚餐时告诉大家，我长大后要当一名作家。

sentences.en: And that's all I've ever wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直想做的事。

sentences.en: But I just love learning, and I love the human mind.
sentences.zh: 但我就是热爱学习，热爱人类的心智。

sentences.en: And so I didn't know that I loved psychology until high school.
sentences.zh: 所以我直到高中才知道自己热爱心理学。

sentences.en: And we had this amazing psychology teacher, Pamela Lynn.
sentences.zh: 当时我们有一位非常棒的心理学老师，帕梅拉·林恩。

sentences.en: And so if she happens to listen to this, she's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 如果她恰好在听这个节目，她真的很棒。

sentences.en: And she taught advanced placement psychology.
sentences.zh: 她教的是大学先修课程（AP）心理学。

sentences.en: And she assigned Oliver Sacks's, the man who mistook his wife for a hat, as summer reading.
sentences.zh: 她布置的暑期阅读书目是奥利弗·萨克斯的《错把太太当帽子的人》。

sentences.en: And I remember reading that and just saying, oh my God, my mind has been blown.
sentences.zh: 我记得读完那本书后，我惊叹道：天哪，我的大脑被震撼了。

sentences.en: You can do this.
sentences.zh: 原来可以这样做。

sentences.en: You can write about this.
sentences.zh: 原来可以写这些内容。

sentences.en: This is ridiculously cool.
sentences.zh: 这简直酷毙了。

sentences.en: And we also read Steven Pinker's, The Language Instinct.
sentences.zh: 我们还读了史蒂芬·平克的《语言本能》。

sentences.en: She assigned, I think, some of the greats who both practiced and were brilliant writers.
sentences.zh: 我想她布置的都是那些既有实践经验又是杰出作家的大家的作品。

sentences.en: So by the time I got to college, I thought, oh, I'm going to register.
sentences.zh: 所以到了上大学的时候，我想，哦，我要去注册课程。

sentences.en: So as you mentioned, I did my undergrad at Harvard.
sentences.zh: 正如你提到的，我在哈佛读的本科。

sentences.en: And I thought, oh, I'm going to register at MIT so that I could take a class with Steven Pinker.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我要去麻省理工学院（MIT）注册，这样就能上史蒂芬·平克的课了。

sentences.en: But luckily for me, he came to Harvard, so I didn't have to do a cross-registration at MIT.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，他后来到了哈佛，所以我不需要去MIT跨校注册。

sentences.en: And he ended up actually becoming my undergrad advisor for my thesis, which was in government and psychology.
sentences.zh: 他最终成了我本科论文的导师，我的论文方向是政府学和心理学。

sentences.en: But I also did creative writing.
sentences.zh: 但我还选修了创意写作。

sentences.en: And I did fiction because I had thought that I was going to be a novelist when I grew up, which did not end up happening.
sentences.zh: 我写的是小说，因为我曾以为自己长大后会成为一名小说家，但这最终没能实现。

sentences.en: But I still love fiction.
sentences.zh: 但我依然热爱小说。

sentences.en: And I love reading fiction.
sentences.zh: 我也热爱阅读小说。

sentences.en: And I hope one day, you know, I have probably, like a lot of writers, I have, you know, the novel in the drawer.
sentences.zh: 我希望有一天，你知道，可能像许多作家一样，我的抽屉里也有一部小说。

sentences.en: And I hope to one day have the time to explore that side more freely.
sentences.zh: 我希望有一天能有时间更自由地探索那一面。

sentences.en: But this was a very long way to say I always wanted to be a writer, but I love people and how minds work and how they think.
sentences.zh: 但说了这么多，其实就是想表达我一直想成为一名作家，但我热爱人类，热爱心智的运作方式以及人们的思考方式。

sentences.en: That's what excites me about writing.
sentences.zh: 这就是写作让我兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: It's what excites me about psychology.
sentences.zh: 这也是心理学让我兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: It's why I wanted to be a fiction writer, because as I've said before in other interviews, I think that the best psychologists are the great novelists and the great poets, because
sentences.zh: 这也是我当初想成为小说家的原因，因为正如我在其他采访中所说，我认为最好的心理学家就是伟大的小说家和诗人，因为

sentences.en: they have had to have such great insight into the human condition to write the way they do
sentences.zh: 他们必须对人类状况有如此深刻的洞察力，才能写出那样的作品，

sentences.en: and to observe the way they do, that oftentimes they reach certain insights that experimental psychology ends up proving, you know, 100 years later.
sentences.zh: 才能进行那样的观察，以至于他们往往能得出一些实验心理学在100年后才证明的见解。

sentences.en: So in your most recent book, The Biggest Bluff, you detail how you became a professional poker player.
sentences.zh: 那么在你最近的书《最大的虚张声势》中，你详细描述了自己是如何成为一名职业扑克选手的。

sentences.en: What made you decide to learn to play Texas Hold'em?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你决定学习打德州扑克？

sentences.en: I understand you didn't even have a deck of cards in your house when you were a kid.
sentences.zh: 我听说你小时候家里连一副扑克牌都没有。

sentences.en: So why that game and not, say, another form of poker or even chess?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么选这个游戏，而不是其他形式的扑克，甚至是国际象棋呢？

sentences.en: That is all because of the great John von Neumann, who was one of the great polymaths of the
sentences.zh: 这全都要归功于伟大的约翰·冯·诺依曼，他是20世纪最伟大的博学家之一，

sentences.en: 20th century, the father of game theory, the father of the computer, one of the fathers of the hydrogen bomb, just an all-around genius.
sentences.zh: 博弈论之父，计算机之父，氢弹之父之一，简直是一位全能的天才。

sentences.en: And in his kind of the foundational text of game theory, the theory of games and economic
sentences.zh: 在他那本博弈论的奠基之作《博弈论与经济行为》中，

sentences.en: behavior, which he co-wrote, he writes about games and talks about the fact that he was looking
sentences.zh: 他与人合著了这本书，他在书中写到了游戏，并谈到他当时正在寻找一种方法来模拟复杂的战略决策，即最高水平的人类决策。

sentences.en: for a way to model complex strategic decision-making, human decision-making at the highest levels.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，他还在为美国国家安全委员会提供咨询。

sentences.en: Now, at this time, he was also advising the Security Council of the United States.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他在讨论当时所有重大的安全问题。

sentences.en: He was, you know, talking about all of the big security issues of the day.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是学术上的探讨。

sentences.en: So this was not merely academic.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，博弈论是以扑克为基础的，他认为国际象棋对于人类决策来说完全是无聊且无关紧要的，因为它是一个

sentences.en: And it turns out that game theory is based on poker and that he dismissed chess as actually being completely boring and irrelevant for human decision-making, because it's a game
sentences.zh: 完美信息博弈。

sentences.en: of perfect information.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你能看到一切的游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a game where you see everything, right?
sentences.zh: 你能看到整个棋盘。

sentences.en: You see the entire board.
sentences.zh: 你能看到所有的棋子。

sentences.en: You see all the pieces.
sentences.zh: 理论上，只要有足够的计算能力，你就能解开它。

sentences.en: And theoretically, with enough computing power, you can solve it.
sentences.zh: 总有一个正确的走法。

sentences.en: There's always a right move.
sentences.zh: 而如果你看看扑克这样的游戏，它更贴近生活，因为它是一个不完全信息博弈。

sentences.en: Whereas if you look at a game like poker, that's much more true to life, because it's a game of incomplete information.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满不确定性的游戏。

sentences.en: It's a game of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满未知的游戏。

sentences.en: It's a game of unknowns.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于人的游戏。

sentences.en: It's a game of people.
sentences.zh: 正如他所写的那样——这是引用他的话——现实生活包含虚张声势，包含试图弄清楚“这个人认为我想做什么”。

sentences.en: As he wrote, and this is a quote from him, real life consists of bluffing, of trying to figure out what does this man think I mean to do?
sentences.zh: 这就是我的理论中游戏的核心所在。

sentences.en: And that is what games are about in my theory.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，这对于心理学来说是一个非常精妙的洞见，而且这位数学家指出：数学是不够的。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, that's just this beautiful insight into psychology and into the fact that here's this mathematician who's saying math is not enough.
sentences.zh: 你知道，计算是不够的。

sentences.en: You know, computation is not enough.
sentences.zh: 国际象棋不是生活，因为生活就像扑克。

sentences.en: Chess is not life, because life is like poker.
sentences.zh: 生活是一个充满未知、充满不完全信息的博弈，你必须做出各种推断，

sentences.en: Life is a game of unknowns, of incomplete information, where you have to make all of these deductions
sentences.zh: 并且必须根据与你博弈的人不断地改变和调整。

sentences.en: and you have to constantly change and adjust based on the people you're playing with.
sentences.zh: 所以数学是不够的。

sentences.en: And so math is not enough.
sentences.zh: 你需要心理学。

sentences.en: You need psychology.
sentences.zh: 这就是博弈论的切入点。

sentences.en: And that's where game theory kind of came in.
sentences.zh: 他想解开扑克之谜。

sentences.en: He wanted to solve poker.
sentences.zh: 他认为如果能解开它，就能找到答案，找到战略决策的关键，从而能够防止核战争。

sentences.en: And he thought that if he could solve it, he would have the answer, the key to strategic decision-making, that he'd be able to prevent nuclear war.
sentences.zh: 真的，我没有夸张。

sentences.en: Really, that's not me exaggerating.
sentences.zh: 而无限注德州扑克是扑克的一种变体，就已知信息与未知信息的平衡而言，它最能反映生活中的决策。

sentences.en: And no limit hold'em is the variation of poker that, in terms of the balance of known to unknown information, best mirrors decision-making in life.
sentences.zh: 因为在其他一些变体中，未知信息太多了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because in some other variations, there's too much unknown, right?
sentences.zh: 底牌太多，私人信息太多，这变得太像赌博了，对吧？

sentences.en: There are too many down cards and too much private information, and it becomes too much gambling, right?
sentences.zh: 变得太像轮盘赌了。

sentences.en: It becomes too much like roulette.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的信息作为依据。

sentences.en: There's not quite enough to go on.
sentences.zh: 而在其他扑克变体中，公共信息又太多了，变得太容易解开了，

sentences.en: And in other variants of poker, there's too much information in common, and it becomes too
sentences.zh: 因为只有一张底牌，其他一切都是可见的，所有其他信息都是公共的。

sentences.en: kind of easy to solve because there's only one whole card, and everything else is visible, and all the other information is in common.
sentences.zh: 所以无限注德州扑克在已知与未知之间达到了一种美妙的平衡。

sentences.en: And so no limit hold'em is kind of this beautiful balance of knowns to unknown.
sentences.zh: 显然，限注德州扑克在已知与未知的比例上是完全一样的。

sentences.en: And obviously, limit hold'em is exactly the same in the sense of knowns to unknown.
sentences.zh: 但如果你谈论的是人生这场游戏，它是一场无限注的游戏。

sentences.en: But if you're talking about the game of life, it's a game of no limit.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在任何特定时刻你都可以下注任何筹码的游戏。

sentences.en: It's a game where you can always wager anything at any given point in time.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一个更好的类比。

sentences.en: So it's a much better analog.
sentences.zh: 所以当我读到这些时，正如你所说，我甚至连一副牌都没有。

sentences.en: So when I read about this, as you said, I didn't even have a deck of cards.
sentences.zh: 我不知道一副牌里有多少张牌。

sentences.en: I didn't know how many cards were in a deck.
sentences.zh: 我对这一切毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: I had zero interest in any of this.
sentences.zh: 但它引起了我的好奇，于是我开始阅读关于扑克的书，我当时就想，就是它了。

sentences.en: But it intrigued me, and so I started reading about poker, and I just thought, this is it.
sentences.zh: 为什么我不学习玩这个游戏，并把它作为一种探索生活中技巧与运气平衡的方式，去学习看看在这个我一无所知的新世界里，我能成为什么样的决策者呢？

sentences.en: Why don't I learn to play this game and use it as a way of exploring the balance of skill versus chance in life, and to kind of learn to see what kind of a decision maker I can
sentences.zh: 在书中，你描述了自己如何将心理学理论和研究应用到

sentences.en: become in this new world that I know nothing about.
sentences.zh: 你的牌局中，然而有时你的行为却违背了你作为心理学家的认知。

sentences.en: So in the book, you describe how you would apply psychological theories and research to
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈心理学在哪些方面影响了你对扑克的研究和实战，以及有时你没有遵循科学原则，结果又如何吗？

sentences.en: your play, and yet sometimes you acted in ways that contravened what you know as a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于任何自以为无所不知的心理学家来说，扑克都是一种当头棒喝。

sentences.en: Could you talk about some of the ways in which psychology informed your study and playing of poker, and then maybe sometimes when you didn't follow the science and how that turned
sentences.zh: 当我学习心理学时，我研究的不仅仅是某个随机课题。

sentences.en: out?
sentences.zh: 我的博士论文是关于不确定条件下的风险决策。

sentences.en: I think that poker is kind of a kick in the pants for any psychologist who thinks they know it all.
sentences.zh: 我研究了自我控制和激烈的情绪状态。

sentences.en: So when I was studying psychology, I didn't just study some random topic.
sentences.zh: 我的导师是已故的伟大心理学家沃尔特·米歇尔。

sentences.en: My dissertation was on risky decision-making under conditions of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 我是他最后一名研究生。

sentences.en: And I looked at self-control and hot emotional conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时在研究交易环境和股市中的自我控制，以及不同的人在压力巨大时会做出怎样的不同决策。

sentences.en: My advisor was the late, great Walter Mischel.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想扑克，我拥有的不仅仅是随机的理论知识。

sentences.en: I was his final graduate student.
sentences.zh: 我拥有的知识直接涉及风险决策和情绪决策。

sentences.en: And so we were looking at self-control in the trading environment and the stock market and how different people would make different decisions with a lot of pressure on them.
sentences.zh: 所以我以为自己能很好地运用这些知识。

sentences.en: And so if you think about poker, I didn't just have random theoretical knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，理论与实践之间存在着巨大的鸿沟。

sentences.zh: 那不是客观的报道，因为他们太擅长让叙事符合他们的需求了。

sentences.en: And they were so good at using their charisma, using their influence, using kind of their appeal to make you see the world from their perspective, that you stopped being objective.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长利用自己的魅力、影响力，利用他们的吸引力让你从他们的角度看世界，以至于你不再客观。

sentences.en: And that scared me, because I wanted to represent the victiMs.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到害怕，因为我想代表受害者。

sentences.en: I wanted to show that these were bad people, because don't, you know, make no two ways about it.
sentences.zh: 我想展示这些人是坏人，因为别搞错了，毫无疑问，

sentences.en: Every single person I write about in the confidence game, all of the con artists are horrible individuals who've ruined lives, right?
sentences.zh: 我在《信心游戏》中写的每一个人，所有的诈骗犯都是毁掉他人生活的可怕个体，对吧？

sentences.en: This nice grandfather card shark, he took advantage by cheating of honest people who wanted to have
sentences.zh: 这位可爱的“祖父”牌手，他通过作弊利用了那些想找乐子的诚实人，

sentences.en: fun and, you know, would go, went to a casino and this guy ran a crooked game and just took all of their money and made them go broke, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们去了赌场，而这家伙经营着一场黑局，卷走了他们所有的钱，让他们破产了，对吧？

sentences.en: These aren't people who deserve it.
sentences.zh: 这些人并不是罪有应得。

sentences.en: These are people who have lost a lot because people have been unscrupulous.
sentences.zh: 这些人是因为他人的不道德而损失惨重。

sentences.en: And that was, you know, one of the fringe examples.
sentences.zh: 那只是，你知道，边缘案例之一。

sentences.en: Other examples are much more egregious.
sentences.zh: 其他的例子要恶劣得多。

sentences.en: Are there characteristics of the people who can be conned that you saw across the many people you studied?
sentences.zh: 在你研究的许多人中，你是否发现那些容易被骗的人有什么共同特征？

sentences.en: I mean, there are a lot of folks who were otherwise incredibly smart who gave millions of dollars to Bernie Madoff, for example.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多非常聪明的人把数百万美元交给了伯纳德·麦道夫（Bernie Madoff），例如。

sentences.en: Oh, for sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that every single person can be conned.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为每个人都可能被骗。

sentences.en: I actually don't think that there's an exception, literally.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为没有例外，字面意义上的没有。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm willing to make a blanket statement like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我愿意做出这样的概括。

sentences.en: I don't think everyone can fall for every con artist or for every con.
sentences.zh: 我不认为每个人都会上每一个诈骗犯或每一个骗局的当。

sentences.en: But I do think there's a con out there for everyone because everyone believes in something and everyone hopes in something and everyone sees the world subjectively.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为每个人都有可能被骗，因为每个人都有信仰，每个人都有希望，每个人看待世界都是主观的。

sentences.en: Even if you're the greatest skeptic of all time, you know, there are still you've got your own pet theories about the world and someone can use that.
sentences.zh: 即使你是史上最伟大的怀疑论者，你知道，你仍然有自己关于世界的理论，而别人可以利用这一点。

sentences.en: Someone who's very, very good.
sentences.zh: 一个非常、非常厉害的人。

sentences.en: Unless you maybe if you lock yourself up in a room, throw away the key and never interact with anyone or meet anyone, maybe you won't be conned.
sentences.zh: 除非你把自己锁在房间里，扔掉钥匙，从不与任何人互动或见面，也许你才不会被骗。

sentences.en: But otherwise, I think everyone is susceptible.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我认为每个人都容易受到影响。

sentences.en: And when you start looking at kind of characteristics, originally, I thought, oh, maybe we'll find that, you know, people are have a lower IQ or are less educated or this or that.
sentences.zh: 当你开始观察各种特征时，起初我以为，哦，也许我们会发现，你知道，人们的智商较低，或者受教育程度较低，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And none of that's true.
sentences.zh: 但这些都不是真的。

sentences.en: So none, there's actually when you're starting to talk about individual differences like that, there's nothing that's predictive at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你开始谈论个体差异时，根本没有任何预测性指标。

sentences.en: But there are a few things that actually make you more susceptible.
sentences.zh: 但确实有几件事会让你更容易受到影响。

sentences.en: And the one that I would say is the biggest factor is not anything about personality or who you are, but where you are in life.
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的因素不是关于个性或你是谁，而是你处于人生的哪个阶段。

sentences.en: So people who are in moments of transition in their life become more susceptible to being conned.
sentences.zh: 所以，处于人生转型期的人更容易被骗。

sentences.en: And so it can be oftentimes it's negative transitions, right?
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，这往往是负面的转型，对吧？

sentences.en: Like a major life change, you know, someone died or you're going through a divorce or you've lost your job or we're going through a pandemic, right?
sentences.zh: 比如重大的生活变故，你知道，有人去世了，或者你正在经历离婚，或者你失业了，或者我们正在经历一场大流行，对吧？

sentences.en: Something terrible has happened.
sentences.zh: 发生了可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Those negative life changes can be huge, but they can be also positive.
sentences.zh: 那些负面的生活变故影响巨大，但转型也可能是正面的。

sentences.en: You know, maybe you got a new job and you've just moved to a new city and you still your sense of stability is gone because everything is new and everything is unknown.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许你得到了一份新工作，刚搬到一个新城市，你的稳定感消失了，因为一切都是新的，一切都是未知的。

sentences.en: Maybe you just had a baby and once again, your world has completely changed.
sentences.zh: 也许你刚生了孩子，你的世界再次发生了彻底的改变。

sentences.en: So when you're in a moment of life change, whether it's positive or negative, even though more often than not, it's negative,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你处于人生变动期时，无论是正面还是负面——尽管大多数时候是负面的——

sentences.en: you become susceptible to con artists because you crave stability and meaning and, you know, something that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 你就会变得容易被诈骗犯利用，因为你渴望稳定、意义，以及你知道的，某种有道理的东西。

sentences.en: And they're very good at providing you with something to lean on with kind of a good story, with a good support at a time when you need it most,
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长在你最需要的时候，用一个好故事、好的支持，为你提供某种依靠，

sentences.en: because they can sense that they can sense that vulnerability and they fill in the blanks that don't actually exist, but they know you want them filled.
sentences.zh: 因为他们能感觉到那种脆弱，他们会填补那些实际上并不存在的空白，但他们知道你希望被填补。

sentences.en: And so they do that for you.
sentences.zh: 所以他们为你做了这些。

sentences.en: A lot of con artists, actually, this is, it's heartbreaking, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 很多诈骗犯，实际上，这很令人心碎，但这是事实。

sentences.en: They'll stalk, you know, these groups of recent widows or, you know, groups of people who've lost their child to some specific disease.
sentences.zh: 他们会跟踪那些刚丧偶的人群，或者那些因某种特定疾病失去孩子的人群。

sentences.en: They'll join these support groups.
sentences.zh: 她们会加入这些互助小组。

sentences.en: There was one con artist who joined this war widows group and she became friends.
sentences.zh: 曾有一个骗子混进了这个战争遗孀互助会，并和大家成了朋友。

sentences.en: This was a very long con with all of these women over the course of a year, two years.
sentences.zh: 这是一场持续了一两年之久的漫长骗局，受害者是这群女性中的所有人。

sentences.en: And then she ended up wiping out all of their savings by individually talking to all of them and giving the sob story.
sentences.zh: 最后，她通过私下与她们每个人交谈，编造悲惨故事，骗光了她们所有的积蓄。

sentences.en: And they all lent her money because she was a friend.
sentences.zh: 因为她是朋友，所以她们都借钱给了她。

sentences.en: And then she disappeared.
sentences.zh: 然后她就消失了。

sentences.en: Much of your writing has focused on risk assessment, whether that's deciding whether to bet or fold or agreeing to give that special fortune teller another $10,000.
sentences.zh: 你的很多著作都聚焦于风险评估，无论是决定下注还是弃牌，还是同意再给那位特别的算命先生一万美元。

sentences.en: So given your study of risk, what have you observed regarding people's risk taking and risk assessment?
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于你对风险的研究，你观察到人们在风险承担和风险评估方面有什么表现？

sentences.en: And how is it playing out during the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 这在疫情期间又是如何体现的呢？

sentences.en: Because we always have to talk about the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 因为我们总是不得不谈论疫情。

sentences.en: Well, we suck at it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在这方面很糟糕。

sentences.en: We're very, very bad for the very simple reasons that, you know, human brains and statistics don't get along, never have.
sentences.zh: 我们非常、非常差劲，原因很简单，你知道，人类的大脑和统计学合不来，从来都不合。

sentences.en: And even statisticians tend to be bad at applying statistics to everyday decisions because that's where we started off this podcast, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至连统计学家在将统计学应用于日常决策时往往也很糟糕，因为这就是我们这期播客的开场，对吧？

sentences.en: Theory versus practice.
sentences.zh: 理论与实践。

sentences.en: You can know it in theory, but that's very, very different from actually internalizing it and feeling it and knowing, you know, what does 1% feel like?
sentences.zh: 你可以在理论上了解它，但这与真正内化它、感受它，并知道“1%是什么感觉”完全是两码事。

sentences.en: Like, what does 10% feel like?
sentences.zh: 比如，10%是什么感觉？

sentences.en: What does 80% feel like?
sentences.zh: 80%是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Which, by the way, is why poker is such a great tool.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这就是为什么扑克是一个如此棒的工具。

sentences.en: Because one of the reasons we're so horrible at statistics in our everyday lives is that the brain learns from experience and from things that have happened to you,
sentences.zh: 因为我们在日常生活中统计学表现如此糟糕的原因之一，是大脑通过经验和发生在你身上、

sentences.en: to someone you know, and not from description, not from what you read.
sentences.zh: 发生在你认识的人身上的事情来学习，而不是通过描述，不是通过阅读。

sentences.en: And our experiences, statistically speaking, are skewed, right?
sentences.zh: 而且从统计学上讲，我们的经验是有偏差的，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not actually representative.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上并不具有代表性。

sentences.en: We don't live in a representative distribution of events.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是生活在一个具有代表性的事件分布中。

sentences.en: And so we tend to, you know, overweight things that we might have personally experienced, underweight things that we haven't personally experienced.
sentences.zh: 所以我们倾向于过度重视我们亲身经历过的事情，而轻视我们没有亲身经历过的事情。

sentences.en: And so we end up with these skewed notions, especially when it comes to small statistics.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们最终会产生这些偏差观念，尤其是在涉及小概率统计时。

sentences.en: You know, what is 1%?
sentences.zh: 你知道，1%是多少？

sentences.en: What is half a percent?
What is 2%?
sentences.zh: 2%是多少？

sentences.en: The best example of the fact that even the best thinkers about this sometimes find it very difficult to use in their everyday life happened at the beginning of the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 最好的例子证明了即使是这方面的顶尖思想家有时也很难在日常生活中运用它，这发生在疫情初期，

sentences.en: a few months in.
sentences.zh: 也就是几个月后。

sentences.en: And when I interviewed Danny Kahneman for the New Yorker Radio Hour, and we talked about kind of since he, you know,
sentences.zh: 当时我为《纽约客》广播时间采访了丹尼·卡尼曼，我们谈到了，因为他，你知道，

sentences.en: won a Nobel Prize for his work on risk assessments and how we think about this.
sentences.zh: 因其在风险评估和我们如何思考风险方面的工作而获得了诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: I was asking about his own kind of thoughts on the pandemic and what was happening.
sentences.zh: 我当时在问他对疫情以及正在发生的事情的看法。

sentences.en: And he told me that in the early days, back in March 2020, he was going to go to Paris for a conference that he had had planned.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，在早期，也就是2020年3月，他原本计划去巴黎参加一个会议。

sentences.en: And this was already, you know, New York was going into lockdown.
sentences.zh: 当时，你知道，纽约已经开始进入封锁状态了。

sentences.en: And he looked at the numbers and he thought, well, you know, these aren't so bad.
sentences.zh: 他看了看数据，心想，嗯，你知道，这些数据看起来没那么糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, it's, oh, the absolute numbers aren't so bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，哦，绝对数值没那么糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, maybe I'm just going to go.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许我还是会去。

sentences.en: And he actually, he didn't cancel the trip and he started packing and was almost ready to go to the airport.
sentences.zh: 他实际上没有取消行程，开始收拾行李，几乎准备去机场了。

sentences.en: And he is older and he's diabetic.
sentences.zh: 而且他年纪大了，还患有糖尿病。

sentences.en: You know, he has a lot of risk factors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他有很多风险因素。

sentences.en: And then it just hit him.
sentences.zh: 然后他突然意识到了。

sentences.en: And he thought, oh my God, you know, exponential growth, right?
sentences.zh: 他心想，天哪，你知道，指数级增长，对吧？

sentences.en: The fact that the absolute numbers are so low right now mean nothing.
sentences.zh: 现在的绝对数值这么低根本说明不了什么。

sentences.en: Let me look at what they were yesterday, the day before.
sentences.zh: 让我看看昨天、前天的数据。

sentences.en: And it just, he said that he was just deeply personally embarrassed for himself that his risk assessment was just completely off.
sentences.zh: 他说他当时对自己感到深深的个人羞愧，因为他的风险评估完全偏离了。

sentences.en: He thought that it wasn't so bad when really it was terrifying because he won the Nobel for understanding this.
sentences.zh: 他以为情况没那么糟，但实际上却很可怕，因为他可是因理解这些而获得诺贝尔奖的人。

sentences.en: But now here he is making his own decision, looking at these numbers, thinking, yeah, you know, let's just go and do this trip.
sentences.zh: 但现在他却在做自己的决定，看着这些数字，心想，是的，你知道，我们还是去旅行吧。

sentences.en: I have already committed to it.
sentences.zh: 我已经承诺要去了。

sentences.en: And so that just goes to show how difficult it is to make those sorts of decisions in everyday life based on those small numbers.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明了在日常生活中基于这些小数字做出那种决定是多么困难。

sentences.en: Now, a poker player actually understands statistics correctly because you've played hundreds of thousands of hands.
sentences.zh: 现在，扑克玩家实际上能正确理解统计学，因为你已经玩过几十万手牌了。

sentences.en: So you've sampled correctly.
sentences.zh: 所以你已经进行了正确的抽样。

sentences.en: So if you know the math, you actually know what 1% feels like.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你懂数学，你实际上就知道1%是什么感觉。

sentences.en: You know what 10% feels like because you've actually sampled it over and over and over and over and you start realizing.
sentences.zh: 你知道10%是什么感觉，因为你已经反复地、反复地抽样了，你开始意识到这一点。

sentences.en: So when people are saying, oh, you know, 1% mortality or something like that, I would say, that's huge.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们说，哦，你知道，1%的死亡率之类的，我会说，那可是巨大的。

sentences.en: You know, I would kill for a 1% edge at the poker table because that means I'm going to eventually take all your money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我愿意为了在扑克桌上获得1%的优势而拼命，因为这意味着我最终会赢走你所有的钱。

sentences.en: You know, 1% is a lot and people, you know, people will study for hours and hours and hours to get an extra half a, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，1%很多，人们，你知道，人们会学习几个小时又几个小时，只为了获得额外的半个，你知道，

sentences.en: half a percentage edge to kind of improve their win rate that much.
sentences.zh: 半个百分点的优势，从而在很大程度上提高他们的胜率。

sentences.en: And you see that when you're a 98.6% favorite to win a hand, you still will lose.
sentences.zh: 当你以98.6%的胜率赢下一手牌时，你还是会输。

sentences.en: And you will lose more frequently than you think you should because nothing's 100%.
sentences.zh: 而且你输的频率会比你认为的要高，因为没有什么事是100%的。

sentences.en: And so you start to feel it viscerally in your gut.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始从直觉上感受到它。

sentences.en: And so that helps you internalize it and make better decisions, better risk assessments in real life.
sentences.zh: 这有助于你内化它，并在现实生活中做出更好的决策和更好的风险评估。

sentences.en: Once again, going back to the pandemic, when I'm on social media, when I'm on Twitter, I actually have my feeds broken up into different lists.
sentences.zh: 再一次回到疫情，当我在社交媒体上，在推特上时，我实际上把我的信息流分成了不同的列表。

sentences.en: So I have my psychology list, I have my poker player list, and, you know, my news liSt.
sentences.zh: 我有我的心理学列表，我有我的扑克玩家列表，还有，你知道，我的新闻列表。

sentences.en: It turns out that in the early days of the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在疫情初期，

sentences.en: the people who saw how serious it was going to be and who actually started taking the most drastic action immediately were the poker players.
sentences.zh: 那些看到疫情将会有多严重，并立即开始采取最激烈行动的人是扑克玩家。

sentences.en: Because they saw the numbers, they understood what they meant, and they acted.
sentences.zh: 因为他们看到了数据，理解了它们的含义，并采取了行动。

sentences.en: Not the psychologists.
sentences.zh: 而不是心理学家。

sentences.en: The psychologists were la-di-da-di-da.
sentences.zh: 心理学家们当时还在漫不经心。

sentences.en: The last event I did before the lockdown was I went to the SPSP convention because they were giving me a media award for journalism,
sentences.zh: 封锁前我参加的最后一个活动是SPSP大会，因为他们要给我颁发一个新闻媒体奖，

sentences.en: and that was during Mardi Gras when the pandemic was starting.
sentences.zh: 那是在狂欢节期间，疫情刚开始的时候。

sentences.en: So they did not cancel that conference.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有取消那个会议。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: But no one knew back then, right?
sentences.zh: 但当时没人知道，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, that was very early days.
sentences.zh: 就像，那是很早的时候。

sentences.en: But at that stage, poker players were already turning around, and I ended up leaving early and canceling.
sentences.zh: 但在那个阶段，扑克玩家们已经开始转变了，我最终提前离开并取消了行程。

sentences.en: I was supposed to go straight from New Orleans to Los Angeles for a poker tournament, and I ended up canceling the trip to Los Angeles and coming back to New York.
sentences.zh: 我本应该从新奥尔良直接去洛杉矶参加一场扑克锦标赛，但我最终取消了去洛杉矶的行程，回到了纽约。

sentences.en: And New York went into lockdown two days after I got back.
sentences.zh: 我回来两天后，纽约就进入了封锁状态。

sentences.en: So that brings me around to your book, Mastermind, and how to think like Sherlock Holmes, because, I mean,
sentences.zh: 所以这让我想到了你的书《Mastermind》，以及如何像夏洛克·福尔摩斯一样思考，因为，我的意思是，

sentences.en: a lot of what you write about there has to do with keeping a lot of this information in our brains, in our mental attic, the things that we keep and the things that we discard.
sentences.zh: 你在书中写到的大部分内容都与将这些信息保存在我们的大脑中、我们的心理阁楼里有关，哪些是我们保留的，哪些是我们丢弃的。

sentences.en: And, you know, you talk about how many of us go through life just looking like Dr. Watson, but not observing like Sherlock Holmes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你谈到我们中有多少人过着生活，看起来像华生医生，却不像夏洛克·福尔摩斯那样去观察。

sentences.en: And it would seem that you used a lot of what you learned writing that book during your stint on the poker circuit.
sentences.zh: 看起来你在扑克圈期间运用了很多你在写那本书时学到的东西。

sentences.en: Do you think that you could have become a champion poker player if you hadn't already written Mastermind?
sentences.zh: 你认为如果你还没有写《Mastermind》，你还能成为一名扑克冠军吗？

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I try not to deal in counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不去处理反事实的问题。

sentences.en: Okay, bad question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 好吧，糟糕的问题，金。

sentences.en: No, I mean, I'm serious.
sentences.zh: 不，我是认真的。

sentences.en: I think it's a counterproductive way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种适得其反的思维方式。

sentences.en: So I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: And I think that in so many different scenarios, you know, biggest bluff wouldn't have been the biggest bluff.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在这么多不同的场景中，你知道，《最大的虚张声势》可能就不会是《最大的虚张声势》了。

sentences.en: And there are so many, so many, you know, I could have chosen a different coach.
sentences.zh: 还有很多很多，你知道，我本可以选择不同的教练。

sentences.en: Something could have gone slightly differently.
sentences.zh: 事情可能会有轻微的不同。

sentences.en: And I could have learned poker just as well with the same coach.
sentences.zh: 我可能也会用同样的教练学好扑克。

sentences.en: And if you think about what actually turned me pro for a few years and what, you know, made this story blow up, it was the fact that I won this major international championship.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想是什么让我真正成为职业选手几年，以及是什么，你知道，让这个故事火起来，那就是我赢得了这个重大的国际锦标赛。

sentences.en: I could have easily not won.
sentences.zh: 我完全可能没赢。

sentences.en: You know, in order to win a title, you have to play with a lot of skill, but you also have to get lucky.
sentences.zh: 你知道，为了赢得冠军，你必须具备高超的技巧，但你也必须运气好。

sentences.en: And I write about in the book, I tried to be very careful because, you know, I was always a researcher and a journalist first and foremoSt.
sentences.zh: 我在书中写到了这一点，我尽量非常小心，因为，你知道，我首先始终是一名研究员和记者。

sentences.en: So I would write down all of my hands during the tournaments, you know, so that I could have a record of what happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我会在锦标赛期间记下我所有的牌局，你知道，这样我就能记录下发生了什么。

sentences.en: And so in the book, I was very careful to note that there were a few moments in that tournament that I won that I should have, quote unquote, lost and been out of the tournament.
sentences.zh: 所以在书中，我非常小心地指出，在我赢得的那场锦标赛中有几个时刻，我本应该，引用一下，输掉并被淘汰出局。

sentences.en: I should have lost all my chips because I got my money in the middle, not as a favorite, but as a dog.
sentences.zh: 我本应该输掉我所有的筹码，因为我把钱投入底池时，不是作为优势方，而是作为劣势方。

sentences.en: You know, I was the one on the bad side of the flip and I got lucky.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是那个翻牌处于不利地位的人，但我运气好。

sentences.en: And so at the final table, there was one hand that I wrote about where I had pocket sevens, I believe, and someone else had pocket aces.
sentences.zh: 所以在决赛桌上，我写到过一手牌，我记得我当时拿着口袋7，而别人拿着口袋A。

sentences.en: You know, that should be it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那本该结束了。

sentences.en: I should be out of the tournament.
sentences.zh: 我本该被淘汰出局。

sentences.en: I ended up making a straight and, you know, not being knocked out and actually doubling my chips and eventually won.
sentences.zh: 我最终凑成了顺子，你知道，没有被淘汰，实际上筹码翻倍，并最终获胜。

sentences.en: And so all of these moments of luck, you know, they conspire to create what ends up being the reality.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些运气的时刻，你知道，它们共同创造了最终的现实。

sentences.en: And so I have no idea, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道，你知道，

sentences.en: I think that writing Mastermind was incredibly beneficial in preparing my mind just to learn well and to learn to take in information and to learn to pay attention.
sentences.zh: 我认为写《Mastermind》在准备我的思维方面非常有益，让我学会如何学习，如何吸收信息，如何学会关注。

sentences.en: And, you know, when I was researching Mastermind, that's when I started meditating.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我在研究《Mastermind》时，我开始冥想。

sentences.en: That's when I actually learned a lot about mindfulness.
sentences.zh: 那时我确实学到了很多关于正念的知识。

sentences.en: And I still, you know, I do that to this day.
sentences.zh: 而且我至今，你知道，我还在这样做。

sentences.en: And I think that that's been immensely helpful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And I think that that's one of the habits that, sure, that did enable me to become good at poker.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这是让我能够擅长扑克的习惯之一，当然。

sentences.en: So a lot of different pieces had to come together to make that possible.
sentences.zh: 所以很多不同的因素必须结合在一起才能实现这一点。

sentences.en: So you just answered the question I should have asked.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚刚回答了我本该问的问题。

sentences.en: It would have been a better question.
sentences.zh: 那会是一个更好的问题。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So are you still playing poker?
sentences.zh: 那么你还在玩扑克吗？

sentences.en: Do you get out there and play?
sentences.zh: 你会出去玩吗？

sentences.en: And do you have to play a lot to stay sharp?
sentences.zh: 你是否需要经常玩才能保持敏锐？

sentences.en: Or have you, you know, kept all the tools handy?
sentences.zh: 还是你，你知道，把所有的工具都放在手边了？

sentences.en: Well, so for the first part of the pandemic, I didn't play at all because I am a live player and everything was shut down.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在疫情的第一阶段，我根本没玩，因为我是现场玩家，一切都关闭了。

sentences.en: And, you know, the last place you want to be is in a casino during a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，疫情期间你最不想去的地方就是赌场。

sentences.en: And then, you know, after I was vaccinated and pre-Delta and pre-Omicron where things started opening up again,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，在我接种疫苗后，在德尔塔和奥密克戎变异株出现之前，情况开始再次好转，

sentences.en: I actually did play and went and played in some events and played in the first World Series that took place since the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我确实玩了，去参加了一些赛事，还参加了疫情以来举办的第一届世界扑克系列赛。

sentences.en: And then kind of stopped playing again with all of the new variants and all of that.
sentences.zh: 然后随着所有新的变异株等等，我又停止了玩牌。

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of it has been informed by what was going on epidemiologically and how I felt about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这很大程度上受到了流行病学情况以及我对此感受的影响。

sentences.en: But I see myself as continuing to play, but not at the level that I was playing before.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我会继续玩，但不会达到我以前玩的水平。

sentences.en: Because I, you know, when I was pro and was part of Poker Stars Team Pro, I mean, I spent eight months of the year on the road.
sentences.zh: 因为我，你知道，当我还是职业选手，是扑克之星职业队的一员时，我的意思是，我一年有八个月在路上。

sentences.en: And that's a lot.
sentences.zh: 那太多了。

sentences.en: And that really took its toll on me.
sentences.zh: 那真的让我付出了代价。

sentences.en: And I'm still and always will be a writer first and foremoSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我仍然，并且永远首先是一名作家。

sentences.en: And at this point, I also see myself as a poker player and I hope to stay in the game and stay involved in, you know, in advocating for and being an ambassador for it.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，我也把自己视为一名扑克玩家，我希望留在游戏中，并继续参与，你知道，倡导它并成为它的形象大使。

sentences.en: Because I think that it's such a great teaching tool.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为它是一个非常好的教学工具。

sentences.en: It's such a great way to learn to make better decisions.
sentences.zh: 它是学习做出更好决策的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: And for women, it's just such a great tool of empowerment, of learning to tap into kind of your inner aggression and to, you know, to hold your own.
sentences.zh: 对于女性来说，它是一个非常好的赋权工具，学习挖掘你内在的攻击性，以及，你知道，坚持住自己的立场。

sentences.en: I think it's helped me be better and more successful in other areas of my life, be stronger, be kind of a less socially acceptable, but more successful version of me, in a sense.
sentences.zh: 我认为它帮助我在生活的其他领域变得更好、更成功，变得更强大，在某种意义上，成为一个社会认可度较低，但更成功的我。

sentences.en: And so, and so I think that's wonderful and I want more women to find it and I feel very strongly about that.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以我认为这很棒，我希望更多的女性能发现它，我对此感觉非常强烈。

sentences.en: So, I will keep playing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会继续玩。

sentences.en: I am still studying and I still try to keep up on it because it does go away if you don't do it and if you don't kind of keep abreast of all of the advances that are happening.
sentences.zh: 我还在学习，我仍然努力跟上，因为如果你不这样做，如果你不跟上所有正在发生的进步，它就会离你而去。

sentences.en: But I don't know if I will ever consider myself a professional player again.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道我是否还会再认为自己是一名职业选手。

sentences.en: I doubt it.
sentences.zh: 我对此表示怀疑。

sentences.en: I think that it will always be semi, you know, either semi-pro or recreational, but it will always be a part of my life.
sentences.zh: 我认为它永远会是半，你知道，要么是半职业，要么是娱乐性质，但它永远是我生活的一部分。

sentences.en: I can really relate to your wanting women to know how to play poker.
sentences.zh: 我真的很能理解你希望女性知道如何玩扑克的心情。

sentences.en: That was something when I was an undergraduate a million years ago, a bunch of us got together.
sentences.zh: 那是我一百万年前读本科时的事了，我们一群人聚在一起。

sentences.en: I went to Barnard, you know, part of Columbia, and we formed something we called Women's Issues Poker.
sentences.zh: 我去了巴纳德学院，你知道，哥伦比亚大学的一部分，我们成立了一个我们称之为“女性议题扑克”的组织。

sentences.en: And we taught ourselves how to play poker because we knew all men would learn how to play poker and women didn't learn how to play poker.
sentences.zh: 我们自学了如何玩扑克，因为我们知道所有的男人都会学玩扑克，而女性却不学。

sentences.en: And we would never have the edge if we didn't know these games.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不懂这些游戏，我们就永远不会有优势。

sentences.en: Good for you.
sentences.zh: 为你点赞。

sentences.en: I'm very happy to hear that.
sentences.zh: 听到这个我很高兴。

sentences.en: So, how do you choose what you want to write about and what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何选择写作主题的？目前正在写些什么呢？

sentences.en: Um, I just follow my curiosity, to give you the honest answer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说实话，我只是追随自己的好奇心。

sentences.en: I never know what I'm going to write about next.
sentences.zh: 我从不知道自己接下来会写什么。

sentences.en: I just, I read a lot and I try to engage with the world as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 我只是大量阅读，并尽可能地去接触这个世界。

sentences.en: And I see kind of what piques my interest and what rabbit hole I go down and which one just won't go away.
sentences.zh: 我会观察什么能引起我的兴趣，我会钻进哪个“兔子洞”，看看哪个念头会一直挥之不去。

sentences.en: And we'll kind of keep popping up over and over and over and those tend to be, you know, my next project.
sentences.zh: 那些不断反复浮现的念头，往往就是我下一个项目的选题。

sentences.en: Right now I'm thinking about my next book, but I'm not, I don't actually, I'm not quite ready to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我现在正在构思下一本书，但我还没准备好谈论它。

sentences.en: But I'm working on a lot of different things.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实在同时做很多不同的事情。

sentences.en: You know, as I said, I studied fiction as an undergraduate and I'm actually flexing those muscles during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 如我所说，我本科时学的是小说创作，疫情期间我正好锻炼了这方面的能力。

sentences.en: I, um, was able to do more exploratory writing.
sentences.zh: 我得以进行了更多探索性的写作。

sentences.en: Um, I ended up working on a TV show, so I was in a writer's room for one year of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我后来参与了一部电视剧的制作，在疫情期间做了一年的编剧。

sentences.en: Um, so that show should be out, um, hopefully next year.
sentences.zh: 那部剧应该会在明年播出，希望如此吧。

sentences.en: Um, and I'm actually doing more screen projects and flexing those narrative muscles.
sentences.zh: 我目前确实在做更多影视项目，也在锻炼叙事能力。

sentences.en: Um, I had, uh, I had an audible original that came out last month called Migraine.
sentences.zh: 我上个月刚出了一部 Audible 原创作品，叫《偏头痛》（Migraine）。

sentences.en: Um, that was about my, it was memoiristic in the sense that it was about my personal experiences with migraine,
sentences.zh: 那部作品带有回忆录性质，讲述了我个人患偏头痛的经历，

sentences.en: but also about the science of it and where we are in kind of treatment and what's going on with that.
sentences.zh: 同时也探讨了相关的科学知识、目前的治疗现状以及相关进展。

sentences.en: And I'm actually working on another audible original, um, about COVID and about the COVID recovery through the lens of Las Vegas, which was the single most affected, um,
sentences.zh: 我目前还在制作另一部 Audible 原创作品，是关于新冠疫情以及通过拉斯维加斯这个视角来看待疫情后的恢复，它是全国受影响最严重的，嗯，

sentences.en: urban area in the country.
sentences.zh: 城市地区。

sentences.en: The unemployment rate went up to 36%, um, because it's all service industry.
sentences.zh: 那里的失业率一度飙升至 36%，因为当地全靠服务业支撑。

sentences.en: Um, so it was just completely devastated.
sentences.zh: 所以它当时完全陷入了瘫痪。

sentences.en: Um, and I ended up spending time there and getting to know kind of some of the people who make Vegas work.
sentences.zh: 我后来在那里待了一段时间，结识了一些让拉斯维加斯得以运转的人们。

sentences.en: Um, and I'm hoping to tell their stories, um, as a way of understanding the human toll that the last few years have taken.
sentences.zh: 我希望能讲述他们的故事，以此来了解过去几年给人们带来的创伤。

sentences.en: Well, Maria Konnikova, this has been just a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 好的，玛丽亚·康尼科娃（Maria Konnikova），和你交谈真是太愉快了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining me on Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你参加我们的《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology）节目。

sentences.en: I really have, uh, enjoyed talking with you.
sentences.zh: 我真的很享受与你的这次谈话。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure, Kim.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴，金（Kim）。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org，或者在 Apple、Stitcher 以及其他任何收听播客的平台上找到《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果你在 Apple 上收听并喜欢我们的节目，请给我们留下评价。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
